claims.text: The target high-entropy alloys have significant atomic disorder.
A Bayesian data-fusion approach will combine first-principles simulations, machine-learning predictions, and experimental measurements.
The proposed approach will explicitly quantify predictive uncertainty.
Disorder-driven phonon scattering is the dominant thermal-transport mechanism within the proposed applicability domain.
Bayesian integration of the multiple data sources will generate a 95% interval for each thermal-conductivity prediction.
Uncertainty quantification will delineate the composition and temperature regimes in which predictions are robust.
Combining simulation, machine-learning, and experimental data will exploit complementary strengths and overcome limitations of single-source conventional models.
Traditional predictive models poorly capture disorder-induced phonon scattering.
The proposed approach will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional methods.
The predicted thermal conductivities and their 95% intervals will align closely with experimental measurements.
Prediction accuracy is expected to improve by approximately 20% relative to conventional models.
The approach will be robust only within the tested composition and temperature ranges.
The approach may perform poorly in regimes where electronic or other additional heat-transport mechanisms dominate.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement will depend on dataset quality, dataset representativeness, and the complexity of alloy disorder.
